resources.string: To help delivery drivers, gig.log reads the screens of the delivery apps you turn on and reads offers aloud while you drive. Screen reading and calculations happen on your phone. Accept and Decline need your tap in gig.log; each automatic tap needs its own permission. If you allow Screen events, gig.log also sees which other app is open. It discards recognized screens with your banking, payment or ID details, or that photograph a document or take a signature, before reading or saving their details. Optional screenshots save the whole screen; your gallery may sync them. Android backup may copy your history and settings.
gig.log doesn\'t sell your data. Android backup and online features can send data off your phone.
gig.log reads offers aloud as you drive. You tap Accept or Decline yourself; automatic taps need your permission.

gig.log reads the screens of the delivery apps you turn on. With Screen events on, it also sees which other app is open. It discards recognized screens with your banking, payment or ID details, or that photograph a document or take a signature, before reading or saving their details. Screen reading and calculations happen on your phone. Customer names and addresses are saved as codes, not as text.

Automatic gas prices start off on a new install; an update keeps your setting. When on, Android's address lookup may send your location to its provider, and the U.S. Energy Information Administration gets a fuel-price request for your region. To stop it, set the bubble's gas price to manual.

Setup sends your vehicle to the EPA for MPG only after you tap "Look up my vehicle", and remembers that choice. Neither lookup sends an account or install ID. The manual MPG search opens Google with your vehicle.

Optional screenshots of the whole screen go to Pictures/gig.log, where gallery sync may copy them. Android may back up your history and settings to your Google account or a new phone, and restore them later; consent records are left out. History and settings stay until you clear them or uninstall, logs keep only recent entries, and screenshots and exports stay until you delete them. More: Privacy details in Settings > Data & privacy > Automation & consent.
Reads offer and tip alerts from delivery apps you turn on.
gig.log reads notifications only from the delivery apps you turn on, and skips other apps\' notifications unread. What it recognizes goes into your history, which Android backup may copy.
Counts your shift miles to estimate profit after vehicle costs.

gig.log uses GPS to count miles only during a shift, which saves battery and collects less location data. If automatic gas prices are on, it may send your last location, even outside a shift, to Android\'s address lookup. Automatic gas prices start off on a new install; an update keeps your setting. To stop them, set the bubble\'s gas price to manual. Your miles stay in your history, which Android backup may copy.

gig.log can tap these buttons in the delivery app for you, depending on the app. Each stays off until you allow it; tap Not now to decide later. Pressing Accept or Decline yourself is your own choice.\n\nEach choice is recorded on this phone with its time, app version and privacy notice version, and left out of Android backup and phone transfer. The app log notes each choice too; it leaves your phone only in a bug report you export. Change them in Settings > Data & privacy > Automation & consent.
